references.text: Jesus predicted his suffering, death, and resurrection while he was in Galilee: 'The Son of Man must suffer greatly … be killed, and on the third day he will be raised' ([ref:Luk 9:22|Luke 9:22]). The angels remind the women of exactly this.

Once again in Galilee, Jesus predicted that 'the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands' ([ref:Luk 9:44|Luke 9:44]). This is part of what the angels remind the women about: what Jesus told them while he was still in Galilee.

Jesus predicted his suffering, death, and resurrection for the third time: he will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, abused, and killed, but 'on the third day he will rise' ([ref:Luk 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33]). Although this prediction was given on the way to Jerusalem (not in Galilee), it is an important part of Jesus' repeated predictions about his resurrection.
Matthew's parallel account at the empty tomb, where the angel says: 'He is not here; he has risen, just as he said' ([ref:Matt 28:6|Matthew 28:6]). The wording is almost identical to Luke's version.
Mark's parallel account at the tomb, where the young man in white clothing says: 'He has risen; he is not here' ([ref:Mark 16:6|Mark 16:6]).

Jesus predicted while he was in Galilee that the Son of Man would be handed over into human hands and killed, but rise on the third day ([ref:Matt 17:22-23|Matthew 17:22-23]). Matthew's parallel to Jesus' prediction about the resurrection in Galilee.

The following verse expands on what Jesus said in Galilee: that the Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinful people, be crucified, and rise on the third day ([ref:Luk 24:7|Luke 24:7]). This is precisely the content of what the angels tell the women to remember.

The risen Jesus himself says that it was necessary for 'the Messiah to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day' ([ref:Luk 24:46|Luke 24:46]). This confirms the fulfillment of what he had spoken about in Galilee.
